description: Seven-valence mechanical discernment of experience-moments. Classifies each new experience-moment against prior attestations on the same experience-story to decide whether to mint a Tier-2 story-point attestation (and which valence it carries). Implements spec §7.3 of 2026-04-18-experience-story-epr-design.md.
contextPrecomputeNote: Rules 5 and 6 need same-status semantics that the DSL cannot express natively (DSL supports literal RHS only, not path-on-both-sides comparisons). Task 3.4 (context-assemble step) MUST precompute two boolean fields before this ruleset runs: priorAttestations.witnessEligible (= moment.status matches priorAttestations.mostRecentStatus AND priorAttestations.computeFingerprintIsNew == true) and priorAttestations.refinementEligible (= moment.status matches priorAttestations.mostRecentStatus AND priorAttestations.hasRicherEvidence == true). These booleans are injected into the priorAttestations context object by the context-assemble step.

rules.rationale: Spec §7.3 rule 1: status is passed AND no prior attestation exists on this experience-story from any compute fingerprint. The system can now do something it could not before. This is the canonical first-time-green event — the story anchor has its first witnessed evidence. Magnitude meaningful because every first-pass is a non-trivial milestone.

rules.when: moment.status == "failed" AND priorAttestations.mostRecentStatus == "passed" AND priorAttestations.errorClassIsNew == true
rules.rationale: Spec §7.3 rule 2 (novel branch): status is failed, prior attestation was passed (green-to-red flip), AND the error class has not been seen in any prior attestation on this story. This is discovery: the system has surfaced a previously-unknown failure mode. Rule 2 is evaluated before rule 3 by design — a @validates-failure-mode scenario that had a prior-passed attestation is correctly classified here as discovery (not rule 3 validation). This is the deliberate ordering from spec §7.3.

rules.when: moment.status == "failed" AND priorAttestations.mostRecentStatus == "passed" AND priorAttestations.errorClassIsNew == false
rules.rationale: Spec §7.3 rule 2 (regression branch): status is failed, prior attestation was passed (green-to-red flip), AND the error class has been seen before in prior attestations on this story. The story has moved backward with a known cause. Rule 2 is evaluated before rule 3 by design — the regression classification takes precedence over the validation classification when a prior passed attestation exists.

Spec §7.3 rule 3: status is failed AND the scenario is tagged @validates-failure-mode. This confirms that the system correctly refuses to do something it should refuse — an expected failure. Rule 3 fires only when rules 2a and 2b did not match (no prior passed attestation, so the green-to-red flip semantics do not apply). The @validates-failure-mode tag is precomputed into the boolean field moment.scenarioTagsContainsValidatesFailureMode by the context-assemble step because the DSL does not support array-contains operations.

Spec §7.3 rule 4: status is passed AND prior attestation was failed (red-to-green flip). The story has recovered — a scenario that was broken is now working again. Valence is progress because recovery represents forward movement, not merely a return to baseline.

Spec §7.3 rule 5: the moment's status matches the most recent prior attestation status AND the compute fingerprint is new for this experience-story (a different validator is seeing the same result). This is independent re-validation: witness valence feeds directly into brit/rakia reach computation (self → community → public). The boolean priorAttestations.witnessEligible must be precomputed by the context-assemble step (Task 3.4) because the DSL does not support path-on-both-sides comparisons: witnessEligible = (moment.status == priorAttestations.mostRecentStatus) AND (priorAttestations.computeFingerprintIsNew == true).

Spec §7.3 rule 6: the moment's status matches the most recent prior attestation status, the fingerprint matches a prior attestation's fingerprint, AND the moment carries materially richer evidence (new sidecar artifact present, duration improvement >20%, or new captured detail). The same compute context is producing better attestations. Magnitude is small because refinement is incremental improvement, not a milestone. The boolean priorAttestations.refinementEligible must be precomputed by the context-assemble step (Task 3.4): refinementEligible = (moment.status == priorAttestations.mostRecentStatus) AND (priorAttestations.hasRicherEvidence == true) AND (priorAttestations.computeFingerprintIsNew == false).
